classification.difficultyReason: Count the supplied intersections, identify the two exact positive sine angles, and translate them by one period to obtain the negative-domain solutions.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The graphs of $y=\sin x$ and $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ are drawn in for $x\in[-2\pi,2\pi]$. Use the diagram to show that there will be 4 solutions to the equation $\sin x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ in this domain.

answer.short: The graphs intersect at four points, so there are four solutions.
answer.worked: Each intersection has the same $x$-coordinate on both graphs, so it satisfies $\sin x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$. There are two intersections in $[-2\pi,0]$ and two in $[0,2\pi]$, giving four solutions.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the exact values of $x$ in this domain.

spec.description: Two sine periods, four supplied blue intersection markers, dashed horizontal comparison line, labelled axes and signed pi ticks. The ordinary dashed guide uses black under house style; the sine series uses standard blue.
spec.answerVisibility: All curves and intersection markers are supplied in the student source; exact intersection abscissae remain hidden.

answer.worked:
Sine is positive in quadrants I and II, with reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{3\pi}{4}\quad\text{in }[0,2\pi],\\x&=\frac{\pi}{4}-2\pi,\frac{3\pi}{4}-2\pi\quad\text{in }[-2\pi,0],\\x&=-\frac{7\pi}{4},-\frac{5\pi}{4},\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{3\pi}{4}.\end{align*}$$
